message.content: {"bid_amount":39,"public_message":"Thirty-nine.","private_thought":"Only p2 left. Short Line mortgages for $100, so any win \u2264$99 is +cash if I mortgage before rolling off Water Works. Bid $39 and keep raising $1 to $99; drop at $100+. Arb improves Park Place survival cushion (max liquid still short of Boardwalk). Never give States."}
message.reasoning:
I need to decide on a bid for SHORT_LINE in the auction.

I will bid $39. This matches the current high bid and continues my strategy of winning Short Line for under $100 so I can mortgage it.

Reconsidering the bid. Buying Short Line for $39 nets about $61 after mortgaging, but p2 could do the same for $38. The real question is whether the railroad is worth more than that cash.

I own States Avenue in the orange group. p2 has four houses on St. James Place, Tennessee Avenue, and New York Avenue. They hold a complete orange monopoly.

States Avenue is in the pink group, not orange. I block p2's pink monopoly there. They also hold a red group and a dark blue group with houses.

I hold the light blue monopoly with three houses on each property. I own Ventnor Avenue, blocking p2 from completing their yellow group. Most other properties are mortgaged.

I own Pacific and North Carolina in the green group, while p2 holds Pennsylvania Avenue. Neither player has a complete green monopoly.

I currently hold Reading Railroad and Pennsylvania Railroad, both mortgaged. If I win Short Line, I would own three railroads total, but only one would be unmortgaged. Mortgaged railroads do not count toward rent multipliers.

Both players face the same arbitrage. Bidding up to $99 nets about one dollar after mortgaging, but above that the cash is lost. The winner gains one dollar; the loser gains nothing.

I should keep raising the bid. Forcing p2 to pay $99 instead of letting them win at $38 nets me $61 while they only gain one dollar after mortgaging. I want to drain their cash.

If p2 mortgages Short Line immediately, they recover the mortgage value and their cash stays flat. Forcing a higher bid does not drain their cash after all. The only way to hurt them is if they keep the railroad unmortgaged and pay rent.

Unmortgaging Reading and Pennsylvania Railroads would yield $100 in rent, but the unmortgage cost is $220. p2 could unmortgage B&O for $110 to reach two railroads at $50 per landing. The real value is the mortgage arbitrage, so both players should bid to $99.

I will bid $39 to match the current high bid. I can raise to $99 and drop if p2 bids $100 or more. They have $225 cash but cannot profitably bid above $99. I am on Water Works and about to act.

I need cash to survive the upcoming rent from p2's properties. Their orange group with four houses each is extremely expensive. St. James Place charges $625, Tennessee Avenue $750, and New York Avenue $800. Their dark blue group with three houses also hits hard: Park Place at $1100 and Boardwalk at $1400.

The red group cannot collect monopoly rent because Indiana is mortgaged. Kentucky and Illinois charge only $18 and $20 in base rent.

My light blue properties with houses generate $400 on Oriental Avenue and $270 on Vermont Avenue.

Connecticut Avenue with three houses pays $300. I have four houses and twelve hotels left to build. I can add one house each to Vermont and Connecticut for $50, or place a hotel on Oriental for $50. Even building requires houses to differ by at most one.

I will build houses on Vermont and Connecticut to four first, then place a hotel. I need the cash to survive their orange and dark blue rent. The spaces after Water Works include Park Place at $1100 and Boardwalk at $1400.

p2 is on Short Line and will finish their turn after the auction. I will roll from Water Works next.

A roll of 9 lands on Park Place for $1100. I cannot pay that with only $546 cash. A roll of 10 hits the Luxury Tax for $75.

Rolling 9 or 11 from Water Works lands on Park Place or Boardwalk, both costing over $1000. That is a one-in-six chance. I need roughly $554 more cash to survive a dark blue hit. I am considering mortgaging States Avenue and Ventnor Avenue, or selling houses on my light blue properties.

Selling all houses on my light blue properties would return $250. Adding the mortgage values of States Avenue and Ventnor Avenue brings total cash to $996. That is still $104 short of the $1100 needed to survive a hit on Park Place. Boardwalk at $1400 is even more unaffordable.

Even with the full liquidation of houses and mortgages, cash would reach $1057. That is still $43 short of the $1100 needed to survive a hit on Park Place.

I verified the dark blue rent values. Park Place with three houses costs $1100 and Boardwalk with three costs $1400. Even after max liquidation and the Short Line arbitrage, cash would still be $43 short. I cannot trade or make deals right now. The auction bid does not prevent bankruptcy on a dark blue landing.

Even if Short Line were free, cash would still be $4 short of the $1100 needed to survive a hit on Park Place. I am checking whether the rent values or house counts are different in this game implementation.

I realized the light blue properties can be mortgaged for $160 after selling their houses. That brings total liquidation to $1156. That is enough to survive a hit on Park Place.

The Short Line arbitrage raises total cash to $1217. That covers Park Place with a $117 surplus, but Boardwalk still costs $183 more than available cash. Mortgaging the light blue properties would destroy the only income engine, so liquidation should be reserved for when landing on Park Place.

I will keep bidding to $99 for the arbitrage. Every dollar of net gain improves my survival cushion against dark blue rent. I do not need to jump bid to scare p2; they have been matching $1 increments for 38 bids and will likely continue.

I will drop the auction if p2 bids $100 or more. At that price the arbitrage becomes zero, and paying $101 to mortgage the railroad would cost me one dollar. I should only bid up to $99.

I will bid $39 to match the current high bid. The public message will be brief: "Thirty-nine." I am weighing whether p2 will drop at $100 or continue bidding to their full $225 cash.
